source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.reading: This CloudHQ facility is in the Northern Virginia cluster spanning Ashburn, Loudoun County, and Prince William County. CloudHQ own corporate site states the company was founded in 2016 by Hossein Fateh, who previously served as CEO and co-founder of DuPont Fabros Technology, an established wholesale data center company. CloudHQ is headquartered at 1212 New York Avenue, Washington, D.C., with regional headquarters in London for EMEA and Singapore for APAC. The company reports a global portfolio of over 5.2 gigawatts of data center inventory, more than 9.2 million square feet of delivered space, more than 1,380 megawatts of contracted critical IT load, and over 330 employees. The fetched company page did not specifically name Loudoun, Prince William, or other Northern Virginia counties, so this registry cluster location is treated as confirmed by the registry itself and the company Washington, D.C. area headquarters rather than by an explicit company statement naming these counties. Care should be taken not to confuse this data center company with an unrelated San Francisco based cloud file synchronization software company that also uses the CloudHQ name. No building specific address or individual MW figures for this particular registry row were located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
CloudHQ MCC2 in Prince William County, Virginia, is operated by CloudHQ, but no IT capacity in megawatts has been published for this facility.

Without a published capacity figure, the facility cannot be sized against other data centers in this collection, or judged for whether it could plausibly host AI training infrastructure, which typically requires tens of megawatts and up. What is on record is the facility's location and operator, not its scale.

No compliance certifications are published for CloudHQ MCC2. That does not mean none exist, only that this site's dataset, built from the operator's own facility page, does not list any, which limits what regulated workloads a reader could confirm the facility is qualified to host.

Virginia has 26 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 20 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 1338.6 MW.
